Lean dot-notation semantics: 'Foo.bar' (explicit or anonymous '.bar' resolved via expected type) requires a literally declared 'Foo.bar' constant; redefining an inductive 'Foo' as 'abbrev/def Foo := ...' removes all its constructors, so any remaining '.bar'-shaped construction site is a hard 'unknown identifier' compile failure, not a warning -- this is a reliable static check (grep for '<TypeName>\.' plus anonymous '.ctorName' at call sites whose expected type unifies to that type) before any inductive-to-def/abbrev redefinition.
